prompt_text:
Here are three proposed solutions [3IDEAS] and their ratings [3IDEARATINGS]. Remove the two lowest-rated ideas and keep and rewrite a compressed summary of ONLY the highest-rated idea including the probability score.
3IDEAS = Here are three distinct solutions:

Fill the 12 liter jug to the brim, then pour the contents of the 6 liter jug into it.  The 12 liter jug will now be full, and the 6 liter jug will be empty.  Empty the 12 liter jug into the 6 liter jug, and you will have 6 liters of water in the 12 liter jug.
Fill the 6 liter jug to the brim, then pour the contents of the 12 liter jug into it.  The 6 liter jug will now be full, and the 12 liter jug will be empty.  Empty the 6 liter jug into the 12 liter jug, and you will have 6 liters of water in the 12 liter jug.
Fill the 12 liter jug with 6 liters of water, then empty it into the 6 liter jug.  The 12 liter jug will now be empty, and the 6 liter jug will be full.  Fill the 12 liter jug with air, then empty it into the 6 liter jug.  The 12 liter jug will now be empty, and the 6 liter jug will be full.

3IDEARATINGS = The first solution is the most elegant, but it requires the most effort.  The second solution is the least elegant, but it requires the least effort.  The third solution is the most difficult to implement, but it has the highest probability of success.  I would assign a 70% probability of success to the first solution, a 60% probability of success to the second solution, and a 90% probability of success to the third solution.

Fill the 12‑liter jug with 6 L of water, pour it into the 6‑liter jug (now full). Empty the 12‑liter jug (now empty) into the 6‑liter jug again (now full). The 12‑liter jug will contain exactly 6 L.
